subproblem.title: Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on a cube
subproblem.statement: For n ∈ ℕ, ρ ≥ 0, every C^1 function φ : (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → ℝ and every i ∈ Fin (n+1): ∫_{[0,ρ]^{n+1}} Dφ(s)(e_i) ds = ∫_{[0,ρ]^n} (φ(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) − φ(insertNth_i(0, s'))) ds'. Here e_i = Pi.single i 1, and insertNth_i(t, s') = Fin.insertNth i t s' is the point whose i-th coordinate is t and whose remaining coordinates, in increasing order, are s'. Both integrals are Lebesgue integrals over the boxes Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ) in Fin (n+1) → ℝ and Fin n → ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 ≤ ρ → ∀ (φ : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → ∀ (i : Fin (n + 1)), ∫ s in Set.Icc (0 : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (fun _ => ρ), fderiv ℝ φ s (Pi.single i 1) = ∫ s in Set.Icc (0 : Fin n → ℝ) (fun _ => ρ), (φ (Fin.insertNth i ρ s) - φ (Fin.insertNth i 0 s))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (h_i∘A is C^1, so by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,ρ], ∫_{[0,ρ]^{m+1}} ∂_{s_i}(h_i∘A) ds = ∫_{[0,ρ]^m} [h_i(A(ρ,s')) − h_i(A(0,s'))] ds'), stated for an arbitrary C^1 function on the parameter cube.

Notation. n ∈ ℕ, ρ ≥ 0, φ : ℝ^{n+1} = (Fin (n+1) → ℝ) → ℝ of class C^1, i ∈ Fin (n+1), e_i := Pi.single i 1. For t ∈ ℝ and s' ∈ ℝ^n, insertNth_i(t, s') := Fin.insertNth i t s' has i-th coordinate t and coordinate succAbove_i(k) equal to s'_k. Write Q_k := Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ) ⊆ ℝ^k with Lebesgue measure (volume), and g(s) := Dφ(s)(e_i).

Proof.
1. (Continuity.) Since φ is C^1, s ↦ Dφ(s) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Evaluating a continuous linear map at the fixed vector e_i is continuous, so g is continuous.
2. (Splitting off coordinate i.) Let E : ℝ × ℝ^n → ℝ^{n+1}, E(t, s') := insertNth_i(t, s'). It is the inverse of the measurable equivalence MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i, and it is measure preserving from volume = volume.prod volume on ℝ × ℝ^n to volume on ℝ^{n+1} (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) i, inverted). E is an order isomorphism (Fin.insertNthOrderIso), so E⁻¹(Q_{n+1}) = [0,ρ] × Q_n (Fin.insertNthOrderIso.preimage_Icc and Icc_prod_eq, exactly as in Mathlib's torusIntegral_succAbove).
3. (Transfer.) Hence ∫_{Q_{n+1}} g = ∫_{E⁻¹(Q_{n+1})} g(E q) dq (MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb) = ∫ g(insertNth_i(t, s')) d((volume restricted to [0,ρ]) ⊗ (volume restricted to Q_n))(t, s'). This uses Measure.prod_restrict and Measure.volume_eq_prod.
4. (Fubini.) G(t, s') := g(insertNth_i(t, s')) is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^n by step 1 and continuity of insertNth (Continuous.finInsertNth). Hence G is integrable on the compact set [0,ρ] × Q_n for the locally finite product Lebesgue measure. By Fubini with the t-integral inside (integral_prod_symm), the integral of step 3 equals ∫_{s' ∈ Q_n} ( ∫_{t ∈ [0,ρ]} g(insertNth_i(t, s')) dt ) ds'.
5. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) Fix s'. The curve t ↦ insertNth_i(t, s') has derivative e_i at every t (hasDerivAt_pi, Fin.eq_self_or_eq_succAbove). Its i-th coordinate is t ↦ t, with derivative 1 = (e_i)_i. Every other coordinate succAbove_i(k) is the constant s'_k, with derivative 0 = (e_i)_{succAbove_i(k)}. By the chain rule, ψ(t) := φ(insertNth_i(t, s')) satisfies ψ'(t) = Dφ(insertNth_i(t, s'))(e_i) = g(insertNth_i(t, s')) for all t. ψ' is continuous, hence interval integrable. Since ρ ≥ 0, ∫_{[0,ρ]} ψ' = ∫_{(0,ρ]} ψ' = ∫_0^ρ ψ' = ψ(ρ) − ψ(0) (integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le, intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt).
6. (Conclusion.) Substitute step 5 for every s' ∈ Q_n into step 4 (setIntegral_congr_fun). This gives ∫_{Q_{n+1}} Dφ(s)(e_i) ds = ∫_{Q_n} (φ(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) − φ(insertNth_i(0, s'))) ds', as claimed. For n = 0, Q_0 is the single point of Fin 0 → ℝ with unit mass, and the identity is the one-variable FTC. Remark: the statement is also the special case f_i := φ, f_j := 0 (j ≠ i) of Mathlib's divergence theorem MeasureTheory.integral_divergence_of_hasFDerivAt_off_countable'. That file (Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DivergenceTheorem) is not in the import closure of the frozen Submission header, so the proof above uses only Fubini and the FTC, which are.
proof_key_steps: g(s) := Dφ(s)(e_i) is continuous because φ is C^1.
The measure-preserving equivalence (t, s') ↦ Fin.insertNth i t s' (inverse of MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove) pulls [0,ρ]^{n+1} back to [0,ρ] × [0,ρ]^n.
Fubini (integral_prod_symm; the integrand is continuous on a compact box) puts the t-integral inside.
FTC in t: d/dt φ(insertNth_i(t,s')) = Dφ(insertNth_i(t,s'))(e_i), so the inner integral is φ(insertNth_i(ρ,s')) − φ(insertNth_i(0,s')).

audit.reason: The exact type matches the stated C¹ cube identity with ρ ≥ 0. Coordinate insertion preserves product volume and identifies the box. Continuity supplies compact-set integrability for Fubini; the insertion curve has derivative Pi.single i 1, and FTC gives the stated endpoint difference. The proof covers n = 0 and ρ = 0 and has no undeclared or circular dependency.

subproblem.title: Integrals over a lattice face as integrals over the parameter cube
subproblem.statement: For all P, d ∈ ℕ, every real ρ, every d-face index G = (w, γ) ∈ LatticeFaceIndex d P (w ∈ ℤ^P, γ : Fin d → Fin P strictly increasing) and every function g : ℝ^P → ℝ, with no measurability or integrability assumption (Bochner integrals): ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} g dH^d = ∫_{[0,ρ]^d} g(Σ_l ρ w_l e_l + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}) ds. Here H^d = μHE[d] on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), e_l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1, and the right side is the integral against Lebesgue measure (volume) on Fin d → ℝ over the box Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ) (G : LatticeFaceIndex d P) (g : Eucl P → ℝ), ∫ x in latticeFace ρ G, g x ∂(μHE[d] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫ s in Set.Icc (0 : Fin d → ℝ) (fun _ => ρ), g (∑ l, (ρ * (G.1 l : ℝ)) • EuclideanSpace.single l (1 : ℝ) + ∑ j, s j • EuclideanSpace.single (G.2 j) (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1-2 of the parent proof (a lattice face is the image of a cube under an isometric affine map, and Hᵈ = μHE[d] on the face corresponds to Lebesgue measure on the parameter cube), specialized to an arbitrary integrand.

Notation. Fix P, d ∈ ℕ, ρ ∈ ℝ (any sign), G = (w, γ) with w : Fin P → ℤ and γ : Fin d ↪o Fin P, and an arbitrary g : ℝ^P → ℝ. No measurability is assumed. The Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0, and every step below is an exact identity of integrals valid for all g. Write e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 for l ∈ Fin P, p := Σ_l (ρ w_l) e_l ∈ Eucl P, and v_j := e_{γ(j)} for j ∈ Fin d. Define L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Eucl P by L(t) := p + Σ_j t_j v_j. For s ∈ Fin d → ℝ let toLp s := WithLp.toLp 2 s ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). Then L(toLp s) = Σ_l (ρ w_l) e_l + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}, which is the point in the right-hand integrand.

Proof.
1. (Coordinates.) For t ∈ ℝ^d and l ∈ Fin P, (Σ_j t_j v_j)_l = Σ_j t_j·[γ(j) = l]. Since γ is injective, this equals t_{j₀} if l = γ(j₀), and 0 if l ∉ range γ. Also p_l = Σ_{l'} ρ w_{l'}·[l' = l] = ρ w_l. Hence L(t)_{γ(j₀)} = ρ w_{γ(j₀)} + t_{j₀}, and L(t)_l = ρ w_l for l ∉ range γ.
2. (L is an isometry.) The family (v_j)_j is orthonormal: it is the orthonormal standard basis (e_l) composed with the injective map γ (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single.comp _ γ.injective). For t, t' ∈ ℝ^d we have L(t) − L(t') = Σ_j (t_j − t'_j) v_j. By orthonormality (Orthonormal.inner_sum), ‖L(t) − L(t')‖² = Σ_j (t_j − t'_j)² = ‖t − t'‖² (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence dist(L t, L t') = dist(t, t'), so L is an isometry and in particular a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding).
3. (Preimage of the face.) The face latticeFace ρ G consists of the x with ρ w_l ≤ x_l ≤ ρ(w_l + 1) for l ∈ range γ and x_l = ρ w_l for l ∉ range γ. By step 1, for l = γ(j) the condition on L(t) reads ρ w_l ≤ ρ w_l + t_j ≤ ρ w_l + ρ, that is 0 ≤ t_j ≤ ρ. For l ∉ range γ it holds automatically. Every j arises as l = γ(j), so L⁻¹(latticeFace ρ G) = {t : 0 ≤ t_j ≤ ρ for all j}. This holds for every real ρ.
4. (The face lies in range L.) Let x ∈ latticeFace ρ G and put t_j := x_{γ(j)} − ρ w_{γ(j)}. By step 1, L(t)_{γ(j)} = x_{γ(j)}. For l ∉ range γ, L(t)_l = ρ w_l = x_l by the face condition. Hence L(t) = x.
5. (Measurability.) latticeFace ρ G is the intersection over l ∈ Fin P of the sets {x : ρ w_l ≤ x_l ≤ ρ(w_l + 1)} (for l ∈ range γ) or {x : x_l = ρ w_l} (for l ∉ range γ). These are closed because x ↦ x_l is continuous, so the face is closed and hence measurable.
6. (Push-forward of Hausdorff measure.) By isometry invariance (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), the push-forward under L of μHE[d] on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is μHE[d] on Eucl P restricted to range L. Since latticeFace ρ G ⊆ range L (step 4), restricting first to range L and then to the face equals restricting to the face (Measure.restrict_restrict_of_subset). Therefore ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} g dμHE[d] = ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} g d(L_*μHE[d]) = ∫_{L⁻¹(latticeFace ρ G)} g(L t) dμHE[d](t). The last equality is the change of variables along the closed embedding L (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.setIntegral_map), valid for every g.
7. (Lebesgue measure on the parameters.) On EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), μHE[d] is the volume measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). The map toLp : (Fin d → ℝ) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is a measure-preserving measurable equivalence from the product Lebesgue measure (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp; measurable embedding (MeasurableEquiv.toLp 2 (Fin d → ℝ)).measurableEmbedding). By MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb, ∫_{L⁻¹(face)} g(L t) dt = ∫_{toLp⁻¹(L⁻¹(face))} g(L(toLp s)) ds. By step 3, toLp⁻¹(L⁻¹(face)) = {s : 0 ≤ s_j ≤ ρ for all j} = Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ).
8. (Conclusion.) Steps 6 and 7, together with L(toLp s) = Σ_l (ρ w_l) e_l + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}, give ∫_{latticeFace ρ G} g dμHE[d] = ∫_{Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ)} g(Σ_l (ρ w_l) e_l + Σ_j s_j e_{γ(j)}) ds, which is the assertion. No case distinction is needed. For d = 0 the steps specialize to the single point p carrying unit mass on both sides. For ρ < 0 and d ≥ 1 both domains are empty.
proof_key_steps: L(t) := Σ_l ρ w_l e_l + Σ_j t_j e_{γ(j)} is an isometry EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ^P, because (e_{γ(j)})_j is orthonormal.
L⁻¹(latticeFace ρ G) = {t : 0 ≤ t_j ≤ ρ for all j} and latticeFace ρ G ⊆ range L (coordinates of L(t), injectivity of γ).

Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives L_*μHE[d] = μHE[d] restricted to range L; restrict to the closed face and change variables along the closed embedding L (IsClosedEmbedding.setIntegral_map).
μHE[d] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), and WithLp.toLp is volume preserving, so the integral becomes the box integral over Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ) in Fin d → ℝ.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree, including arbitrary real ρ and arbitrary integrands. Coordinates establish the precise preimage and range inclusion; orthonormality gives the isometry. Closed-embedding change of variables applies without measurability or integrability hypotheses, and WithLp transport correctly distinguishes Euclidean from function-space parameters. Zero dimension and nonpositive ρ are covered. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Stokes' theorem on the parameter cube of a lattice face
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, F = (z, α) ∈ LatticeFaceIndex (m+1) P, and let ω be a smooth (C^∞) m-form on ℝ^P (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m with IsSmoothForm ω). Put e_l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1, p = Σ_l ρ z_l e_l, A(s) = p + Σ_j s_j e_{α(j)} for s ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, α_i = α ∘ succAbove_i (= (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i).trans α) and u_i = (e_{α_i(0)}, …, e_{α_i(m−1)}). Then ∫_{[0,ρ]^{m+1}} dω(A(s))(e_{α(0)}, …, e_{α(m)}) ds = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i ( ∫_{[0,ρ]^m} ω(Σ_l ρ (z + e_{α(i)})_l e_l + Σ_j s'_j e_{α_i(j)})(u_i) ds' − ∫_{[0,ρ]^m} ω(p + Σ_j s'_j e_{α_i(j)})(u_i) ds' ). Here z + e_{α(i)} = z + Pi.single (α i) 1 ∈ ℤ^P, and all integrals are Lebesgue integrals over Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ) in Fin (m+1) → ℝ, respectively Fin m → ℝ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 5 and 6 of the parent proof (exterior-derivative expansion, chain rule, identification of the opposite faces), carried out on the parameter cube. Step 4 (Fubini/FTC) is supplied by the sibling lemma br_cube_integral_fderiv_eq_faces.

Notation. P, m ∈ ℕ, ρ > 0, F = (z, α) with z : Fin P → ℤ and α : Fin (m+1) ↪o Fin P, and ω : ℝ^P → (continuous alternating m-linear maps) of class C^∞. Let e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1, v_j := e_{α(j)} for j ∈ Fin (m+1), and p := Σ_l (ρ z_l) e_l. Let DA : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^P be the continuous linear map s ↦ Σ_j s_j v_j (= Σ_j proj_j.smulRight v_j), and A(s) := p + DA(s), the point in the left integrand. For i ∈ Fin (m+1) let α_i := (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb i).trans α, so α_i(j) = α(succAbove_i j) definitionally. Let u_i := (e_{α_i(0)}, …, e_{α_i(m−1)}); this is removeNth_i(v), since Fin.removeNth i v j = v (succAbove_i j) by definition. Further let h_i(y) := ω(y)(u_i) for y ∈ ℝ^P, φ_i := h_i ∘ A : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ, ε_i := Pi.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, and Q_k := Set.Icc 0 (fun _ => ρ) ⊆ ℝ^k.

Proof.
1. (Regularity.) ω is C^∞, hence differentiable everywhere. Evaluation at the fixed tuple u_i is a continuous linear map on continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply), so h_i is C^∞ and in particular C^1. A = p + DA is affine, with HasFDerivAt A DA s at every s, and is C^1. Hence φ_i = h_i ∘ A is C^1.
2. (Chain rule.) DA(ε_i) = Σ_j (ε_i)_j v_j = v_i. Hence Dφ_i(s)(ε_i) = Dh_i(A(s))(DA ε_i) = Dh_i(A(s))(v_i) for every s.
3. (Exterior derivative.) By exteriorDerivative_apply (Mathlib extDeriv_apply; ω is differentiable at A(s)), for every s: dω(A(s))(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i • D(y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth_i v))(A(s))(v_i) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dh_i(A(s))(v_i). The integer power (−1 : ℤ)^i acting by • equals multiplication by (−1 : ℝ)^i. With step 2, dω(A(s))(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dφ_i(s)(ε_i).
4. (Integrate over Q_{m+1}.) Each s ↦ (−1)^i Dφ_i(s)(ε_i) is continuous because φ_i is C^1, hence integrable on the compact box Q_{m+1}. So the integral of the finite sum is the sum of the integrals (integral_finset_sum), and constants factor out (integral_const_mul): ∫_{Q_{m+1}} dω(A(s))(v) ds = Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{Q_{m+1}} Dφ_i(s)(ε_i) ds.
5. (Fubini and FTC.) Apply br_cube_integral_fderiv_eq_faces with n := m, the same ρ (0 ≤ ρ since ρ > 0), φ := φ_i (C^1 by step 1) and coordinate i. This gives ∫_{Q_{m+1}} Dφ_i(s)(ε_i) ds = ∫_{Q_m} (φ_i(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) − φ_i(insertNth_i(0, s'))) ds', where insertNth_i(t, s') := Fin.insertNth i t s'. For c = ρ and c = 0, s' ↦ φ_i(insertNth_i(c, s')) is continuous (Continuous.finInsertNth), hence integrable on the compact box Q_m. So (integral_sub) the right side equals ∫_{Q_m} φ_i(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) ds' − ∫_{Q_m} φ_i(insertNth_i(0, s')) ds'.
6. (Identification of the opposite faces.) Let t ∈ ℝ and s' ∈ ℝ^m. Split Σ_{j ∈ Fin(m+1)} at j = i (Fin.sum_univ_succAbove) and use insertNth_i(t, s')_i = t and insertNth_i(t, s')_{succAbove_i k} = s'_k (Fin.insertNth_apply_same, Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove). This gives A(insertNth_i(t, s')) = p + t v_i + Σ_k s'_k e_{α(succAbove_i k)} = p + t v_i + Σ_k s'_k e_{α_i(k)}. For t = 0 this is p + Σ_k s'_k e_{α_i(k)}, the point in the second integral of the i-th summand. For t = ρ: the lattice point z + Pi.single (α i) 1 has coordinates z_l + [l = α(i)], and the cast ℤ → ℝ is additive. So Σ_l ρ (z + Pi.single (α i) 1)_l e_l = Σ_l (ρ z_l) e_l + Σ_l ρ [l = α(i)] e_l = p + ρ e_{α(i)} = p + ρ v_i. Hence A(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) = Σ_l ρ (z + Pi.single (α i) 1)_l e_l + Σ_k s'_k e_{α_i(k)}, the point in the first integral. Finally, φ_i(insertNth_i(c, s')) = ω(A(insertNth_i(c, s')))(u_i), and u_i = (e_{α_i(0)}, …, e_{α_i(m−1)}) is exactly the frame in the right-hand integrands.
7. (Conclusion.) Combine steps 4, 5 and 6 with (−1)^i a − (−1)^i b = (−1)^i (a − b). This gives ∫_{Q_{m+1}} dω(A(s))(v) ds = Σ_i (−1)^i ( ∫_{Q_m} ω(Σ_l ρ (z + Pi.single (α i) 1)_l e_l + Σ_k s'_k e_{α_i(k)})(u_i) ds' − ∫_{Q_m} ω(p + Σ_k s'_k e_{α_i(k)})(u_i) ds' ), which is the assertion. For m = 0 the frames u_i are empty, Q_0 is a point of unit mass, and the identity reads ∫_0^ρ dω(p + s v_0)(v_0) ds = ω(p + ρ v_0)() − ω(p)().
proof_key_steps: h_i(y) := ω(y)(e_{α∘succAbove_i}) is C^∞, φ_i := h_i ∘ A is C^1, and Dφ_i(s)(e_i) = Dh_i(A(s))(e_{α(i)}) by the chain rule, since DA(e_i) = e_{α(i)}.
exteriorDerivative_apply gives dω(A s)(e_α) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dφ_i(s)(e_i); continuous integrands allow swapping the finite sum with the box integral.
Apply br_cube_integral_fderiv_eq_faces to each φ_i, then split the face integral (continuous integrands on a compact box).
A(insertNth_i(ρ, s')) = Σ_l ρ (z + e_{α(i)})_l e_l + Σ_j s'_j e_{α_i(j)} (because ρ(z + e_{α(i)}) = ρz + ρe_{α(i)}), and A(insertNth_i(0, s')) = p + Σ_j s'_j e_{α_i(j)}.
